items.streamTitle: A simulated X ranking rule amplified low-credibility links through easy reactions
items.streamSummary: In their model, predicted likes and reposts could substitute for replies and quotes in a weighted engagement score, favoring content that elicited quick reactions. Weight tuning had little or adverse effect in simulations; a threshold requiring predicted reflective engagement reduced the low-credibility exposure gap without reducing modeled mainstream exposure or engagement. This is an unreviewed preprint and a calibrated reimplementation, not a live platform intervention. A ranking system can shape exposure through the way it combines behavior signals, even if no single signal is explicitly labeled as misinformation. Platform-level causal claims require live validation and careful treatment of source-credibility labels.

items.streamTitle: A Canadian climate-news corpus provides frame labels with category-level reliability
items.streamSummary: On a 1,000-sentence independently double-coded reference set, the pooled macro F1 was 0.866, while mean per-category macro F1 was 0.773; categories were assigned A/B/C reliability tiers. These metrics describe annotation performance, not proof of media effects on public opinion. Coverage is Canadian and source selection matters. The corpus is a useful design pattern for PSYWERX discourse maps: publish a taxonomy, human coding reference, category-specific uncertainty, and reusable data together. Trend analyses should account for changing outlet coverage and weaker classes.

items.streamTitle: Selective human review can make AI-assisted hypothesis tests cheaper while controlling error
items.streamSummary: The authors prove finite-sample validity under their model and show near-optimal asymptotic cost as target errors tighten. Numerical studies found the largest savings when cheap AI reports and selective human checks both contributed. These are formal and simulated results, not evidence of savings or accuracy in a deployed PSYWERX review queue. Human review is most useful where the AI report changes the value of verification. A pilot with paired human and AI labels would be needed to estimate the error model and test whether the theoretical saving transfers to an actual research workflow.

items.streamTitle: LLM conversation judges needed anchors to make their scores comparable
items.streamSummary: Pointwise scores correlated moderately with human ratings, while pairwise comparisons suffered from long transcripts and position bias. The new dataset showed a gap between current judges and human discrimination. Calibration placed judges on a shared scale and transferred to the human-AI dataset in their tests; it did not make the judges equivalent to human evaluators. Evaluation scores should carry a calibration protocol and a human reference. In PSYWERX-style human-AI assessments, compare stable anchor cases and inspect order effects before treating score differences as substantive.

items.streamTitle: NATO framed interoperability as preparation that must precede multi-domain operations
items.streamSummary: The publication lays out an operational approach and implementation logic: interoperability and resilience must be built and exercised before crisis, while nations retain authority over what they share. It reports no controlled comparison or measured advantage from a new deployment. Its discussion of the cognitive dimension is conceptual rather than an observed influence effect. For information advantage, speed is an end-to-end property of sensing, sharing, deciding, and acting, subject to governance and trust. Evaluation should test degraded communications, data-sharing permissions, and cross-national handoffs rather than count connected tools alone.

items.streamTitle: Food-package claims often highlighted one nutrient while missing overall quality
items.streamSummary: Products with claims sometimes had more favorable profiles in aggregate, but the pattern varied. Foods with trans-fat claims and beverages with sodium claims often scored worse than peers without them; many claim-bearing products still counted as less healthy overall. The study measured products, not how consumers interpreted labels or changed purchases. A salient attribute can be an imperfect proxy for the full outcome. Communication and evaluation should distinguish the specific true claim from the broader inference audiences may draw; behavioral effects need separate testing.

items.streamTitle: Moral disengagement preceded self-interested choices in costly environmental tradeoffs
items.streamSummary: Positive beliefs about greed and moral disengagement were associated with more self-interested, environmentally harmful choices. Disengagement was relatively stable before and after a choice, and shaped emotional reactions. Several studies were correlational, so the paper does not establish that changing disengagement would cause a different real-world choice. The same stated environmental concern can coexist with different norms about self-interest and different emotional responses. Assess these factors alongside actual costs; avoid assuming a post-choice justification is the only mechanism or that a vignette predicts sustained behavior.

items.streamTitle: Spoken claims remained harder for AI to verify than the same claims in text
items.streamSummary: Mazumder and colleagues built VeriSpeak, a benchmark of 3,879 spoken claims about temporal, geographic, and relational facts, balanced between true and false labels. They tested large audio-language models with retrieval and explicit claim-evidence reasoning. The authors report a persistent text-to-speech performance gap. Retrieval alone gave limited gains because models sometimes conflated evidence with the spoken claim; retrieval plus explicit reasoning performed better, with one reasoning-tuned model reaching 86.1% accuracy. The benchmark uses controlled factual claims, so these results do not establish reliability on noisy political speeches or real-time podcasts. Audio fact checking needs more than transcription plus retrieval. Test claim extraction, evidence comparison, and speech-specific errors separately before using a system to label live influence content.

items.streamTitle: Video-agent hallucination depended strongly on whether the right moment was retrieved
items.streamSummary: In those tested systems, grounding had roughly four times the downstream causal impact of corrupted visual observations. Finding the right region mattered more than tight temporal overlap, and wrong evidence caused more harm than missing evidence. Stage benchmark scores did not consistently predict these cascading effects. The preprint's controlled interventions do not show the same proportions for every video system or field workflow. For video-based incident analysis, log which segment a model used and audit retrieval failures separately from final answer quality. A high aggregate score can hide a failure in the evidence path.

items.streamTitle: Groups improved only when people could tell which peers were actually performing well
items.streamSummary: An online immersive experiment with 621 participants found that groups did not automatically outperform individuals in a dynamic tracking task. Groups performed better only when members could see others’ payoffs and selectively weight cues from peers who were doing well; location-only social information could even hurt performance, especially in fast-changing conditions. Movement models and agent-based simulations supported the same mechanism. The experiment did not show groups surpassing the best individual, and the task is artificial, but it offers a concrete lesson for collective decision systems: information quality and selective weighting matter more than social connectivity alone.

items.streamTitle: Political polarization was tied much more strongly to electric-vehicle adoption than to rooftop solar in Germany
items.streamSummary: A new Nature Sustainability study combined three survey waves with clean-technology and election records from more than 10,000 German municipalities. AfD supporters were much less likely to report electric-vehicle adoption or intent than Green-party supporters, while the partisan gap for rooftop solar was smaller. Municipality panel models likewise linked rising AfD support to lower subsequent adoption. An instrumental-variable analysis using wolf attacks as a source of vote-share variation pointed in the same direction, but its estimates apply to a specific subset of municipalities and were sensitive to some restrictions. The study suggests technologies can acquire different political meanings even within the same climate domain.

items.streamTitle: A low-barrier RAG setup made a mainstream LLM confidently present fringe science as authoritative
items.streamSummary: Researchers built two Custom GPTs around GPT-5.1 and supplied each with ten fringe physics papers plus instructions to treat that material as authoritative. Without retraining or changing model weights, the resulting systems produced fluent, detailed answers that domain experts often judged seriously misleading, while the unmodified model stayed closer to mainstream science. The study is a deliberate demonstration in two narrow physics domains, not a prevalence estimate for deployed RAG systems. Its broader importance is provenance: a polished answer can remain linguistically convincing even when the retrieval corpus and instructions have quietly redirected what the model treats as knowledge.
items.attribution: Collins et al. — AI and Ethics

items.streamTitle: First-time parents’ emotional dynamics changed with who was on leave—and with whether partners were together
items.streamSummary: A Danish experience-sampling study tracked first-time parents’ emotions six times daily across maternity- and paternity-leave periods. Partners who were physically together showed synchronized valence and arousal, while randomly paired couples did not. Regulation patterns also changed with leave roles: arousal had a stronger regulatory role for the parent not on leave, and mothers’ responses to fathers differed between maternity and paternity leave. Substantial couple-level variation remained. The study is observational, so leave arrangements cannot be treated as experimentally causal, but it shows why close relationships are better modeled as interacting systems than as two isolated individuals.

items.streamTitle: Banking records showed signs of severe financial instability years before many abuse disclosures
items.streamSummary: A Nature study examined up to seven years of banking records for 5,428 women who disclosed domestic or financial abuse and 15,602 matched controls. Victim-survivors had lower savings and credit scores, more missed payments and debt pressure, and distinctive changes in spending and account management; many differences appeared years before disclosure. The study is observational, self-disclosure may select more severe cases, and some controls may also have experienced undisclosed abuse. The findings show the value of longitudinal administrative data for understanding vulnerability, but they do not justify turning transaction patterns directly into an automated abuse label.

items.streamTitle: A Special Operations Chinook landed and replenished on an autonomous barge in a first publicly disclosed demonstration
items.streamSummary: Naval News reports that a U.S. Army 160th Special Operations Aviation Regiment MH-47G Chinook landed and conducted replenishment operations from an autonomous Sea Machines barge. The demonstration suggests a potential way to create distributed maritime refuel or logistics nodes without a conventional crewed ship. Public reporting does not provide sea-state limits, operator-intervention rates, safety margins, throughput, or contested-environment performance, so it should not be treated as proof of operational readiness. The real value of the concept will depend on whether autonomous logistics can remain reliable, survivable, and recoverable when communications and operating conditions degrade.
items.attribution: Sea Machines Robotics — via Naval News

items.streamTitle: A new behavioral-research protocol combines DAGs and nonlinear models to move from “did it work?” toward “how did it work?”
items.streamSummary: BriDGE is a new methodological protocol for analyzing mechanisms inside randomized behavioral experiments. It combines explicit DAG-based assumptions, causal-discovery tools, generalized additive models for nonlinear pathways, mediation analysis, bootstrapping, sensitivity checks, and simulation-based power planning. Simulation and semi-synthetic tests show that the workflow can recover complex pathways under known data-generating conditions. The authors also emphasize the key limitation: in real trials, the true causal graph is unknown, so causal discovery cannot validate itself. The framework is therefore best used to make mechanism assumptions and tests more explicit—not to replace identification logic with an algorithm.

items.streamTitle: The UK and U.S. paired a new AI-autonomy partnership with the first torpedo firing from a British uncrewed undersea vehicle
items.streamSummary: The UK and United States announced a new defense AI and autonomy partnership between their rapid-delivery organizations, aimed at producing trusted, interoperable capabilities for areas such as critical-infrastructure protection. The announcement came alongside a concrete technical milestone: a British 12-metre Excalibur uncrewed undersea vehicle fired a U.S.-Australian heavyweight torpedo in UK waters, reportedly the first such launch by either country from an uncrewed underwater vessel. The demonstration proves integration and firing in a test, not combat effectiveness. The deeper issue is allied interoperability across software, autonomy, weapons, command, and safety controls.
items.attribution: UK Prime Minister’s Office / Ministry of Defence

items.streamTitle: Texas froze data-center permits while regulators audit a project queue larger than five times the state’s record peak demand
items.streamSummary: Texas has halted state permits for data centers until grid and water regulators complete a broader audit of the sector. ERCOT has more than 474 gigawatts of data-center interconnection requests under consideration—over five times the state’s record peak electricity demand—and state officials want projects to document power, water, infrastructure costs, and other impacts before approvals proceed. The 474-gigawatt queue is not a forecast of actual future load; it can include speculative and overlapping projects. The development shows AI infrastructure becoming a coupled policy problem spanning compute growth, grid reliability, water, cost allocation, and local resilience.

items.streamTitle: DARPA is evaluating autonomous trauma surgery as a progression from component skills to human teaming to independence
items.streamSummary: DARPA has launched a $3.5 million competition for trauma-surgery robotics and held its Industry Day on September 22. The evaluation structure is notable: systems first face component gates for medical knowledge, physical capability, and rapid learning, then separate lanes test collaboration with a human surgeon and independent assessment, planning, and execution. No performance results exist yet; the scored competition is planned for March 2027. The program is therefore not evidence that autonomous surgery is ready. Its immediate value is methodological—a staged TEVV framework that distinguishes prerequisite skills, human-machine teaming, and true independent capability.

items.streamTitle: A multi-level school program improved several precursors of adolescent help-seeking, while actual behavior was more mixed
items.streamSummary: A randomized trial with 174 Iranian high-school girls tested a six-session mental-health program built around individual, social, and ecological barriers to seeking help. The intervention group improved over time in life satisfaction, help-seeking intention, recognition of need, perceived social support, and mental-health literacy. Actual help-seeking behavior and coping showed significant group-by-time differences, but their overall between-group effects were not statistically significant. Because the program bundled several components and involved only female adolescents in one national context, the study cannot identify which ingredient drove the gains or how well the results generalize elsewhere.

items.streamTitle: Rhesus monkeys adjusted decision control in a pattern consistent with metacognitive monitoring
items.streamSummary: A new rhesus-macaque study examined accuracy, difficulty, and response time in a two-choice task. After accounting for difficulty, the monkeys were actually more accurate on faster-response trials, contrary to a simple speed–accuracy tradeoff. A computational model explained the pattern by assuming that a supervisory process weighs the cost of cognitive control against the confidence benefit of investing more effort. The result is consistent with metacognitive regulation outside humans, but it is behavioral and model-based evidence; it does not directly show subjective awareness or identify a specific neural monitoring mechanism.

items.streamTitle: The UK is creating a National Centre for Information Defence to detect, attribute, and disrupt hostile-state influence operations
items.streamSummary: The UK government has tasked security chiefs to create a National Centre for Information Defence focused on detecting, attributing, and disrupting hostile-state information attacks. Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced the center in his September 22 UN address, framing disinformation, deepfakes, cyber activity, and AI-enabled manipulation as threats to democratic and social resilience. The announcement establishes a new institutional capability, not evidence that it will reduce influence operations. Key details—including authorities, staffing, performance measures, attribution standards, and how disruption effects will be assessed—have not yet been publicly demonstrated.

items.streamTitle: In simulated crowd control, agent speed mattered far more than the vote-aggregation rule
items.streamSummary: Across 8,010 simulations of crowd-sourced continuous control, agent speed explained much more tracking-error variance than the method used to aggregate participant votes. In the main factorial analysis, speed accounted for 46–97% of variance versus 2–29% for aggregation method, with a median variance ratio of 6.9 to 1. Performance often followed a U-shaped curve because slow agents struggled to recover from delayed corrections while fast agents overshot on stale headings. These are simulation results under specific controller and delay assumptions, not evidence from human crowds or deployed robots.

items.streamTitle: Children reached similar generalizations through different strategies as they got older
items.streamSummary: A study of 84 children aged 4, 6, and 8 compared four common generalization tasks and found that performance improved with age, but the tasks did not clearly behave like one shared ability. In transitive inference, younger children often succeeded without accurate memory for the learned pairs, and computational modeling suggested a value-based reinforcement-learning strategy; 8-year-olds relied more on pair memory. The study therefore shows that the same correct answer can reflect different cognitive processes. Some tasks had floor or ceiling effects, so the degree of cross-task independence remains uncertain.
